intro: 104 AI items this week (68 India-relevant) across 9 sources.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
items.summary: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare to unify clinical data and automate workflows. Reduce administrative burnout. See how it works.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a new lightweight model for agent execution
items.summary: At 10 cents per million input tokens, Ember is significantly cheaper than frontier competitors like Haiku and Luna.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.summary: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash brings native 15-second video generation and editing, stronger consistency, and 30% lower pricing.

items.title: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
items.summary: Anthropic says the new models "show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision," as well as in communicating more clearly with users.

items.title: From the front row to the hot seat — what the midterms mean for Big Tech
items.summary: After spending two years getting cozy with the White House, Big Tech is suddenly trying to make friends with Democrats, and the open question is whether that image makeover can hold up against what states, local communities, and the markets are about to do.

items.title: A Closer Look at Phonon TTS. Launching High-Quality On-Device Speech That Tops the Benchmarks.
Automattic debuts a platform to deploy vibe-coding apps amid a changing internet
items.summary: Automattic aims to compete with the likes of Lovable with Spacefast.

items.title: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
items.summary: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal…

items.title: Cyberattacks threaten to make open-source AI a little less open, Hugging Face exec warns
items.summary: Hugging Face executive Irene Solaiman warns that growing cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force tighter security restrictions, threatening the accessibility that makes open-source communities valuable to developers worldwide.

items.title: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+ languages
items.summary: Otter AI just added support for 27 languages and revealed an upcoming feature that can follow along if speakers switch between languages.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
items.summary: The AI company is expected to set its valuation range this week, the Wall Street Journal reported.

items.title: Jensen Huang reportedly engaged a PR firm with a history of handling high-profile sex scandals a year ago
items.summary: The PR firm was enlisted shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report described Alice Huang's business dealings with Jensen Huang, Wired reported.

items.title: A short seller flagged Nvidia CEO’s ties to a suspected Chinese spy six months before the scandal
items.summary: Six months before Nvidia's spy scandal erupted, Culper Research was already questioning Jensen Huang's unusually close relationship with a Chinese executive.

items.title: The race is on to sue Nvidia
items.summary: Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% after its board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and one securities law expert says the company’s earlier insistence that it was all “normal” could turn into a very expensive problem.

items.title: Jensen Huang pulls out of ElevenLabs Summit amid Nvidia controversy
items.summary: The Nvidia CEO also pulled out of an Anthropic event earlier.

items.title: Israeli AI security startup Bay raises $50 million
items.summary: Bay says it addresses a primary barrier to AI adoption by "allowing autonomous agents to perform business-critical work safely while enterprises retain control and accountability at scale".

items.title: Cognizant commits over 25,000 professionals to Anthropic's Claude delivery
items.summary: The group is focused on execution excellence, transformation and client success, with the scale to take AI from pilot to production across enterprises' core operations, the Nasdaq-listed IT company said.

items.title: Froncort.AI Raises $2.3 Mn From Google.org To Expand AI-Based Disease Surveillance
items.summary: Healthcare AI startup Froncort.AI has secured $2.3 Mn (₹21.5 Cr) in fresh capital from Google’s philanthropic arm, Google.org, to scale…

items.title: Anthropic targets valuation of about $1 trillion in IPO
items.summary: Anthropic has entered into agreements with partners AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC, who will purchase $26.0 billion of its Class N common stock in a private placement.

items.title: TSMC October Revenue Hits Record $17.81 Bn on Skyrocketing AI Chip Demand
items.summary: TSMC's October revenue rose 59.7% year-on-year, as demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing continues to drive growth, contrasting with recent volatility

items.title: Froncort.AI Gets $2.3M From Google.org to Expand AI-Based Disease Screening in India
items.summary: Froncort.AI has received funding from Google.org to enhance its AI disease screening platform in India, aiding health workers in identifying risk areas.

items.title: Is AI-Powered Reverse Engineering the Death of Proprietary Software?
items.summary: Explore how AI-powered reverse engineering challenges proprietary software norms and the implications for intellectual property in 2024.

items.title: OpenAI unveils a 'Control Room' safety feature that shuts down AI agents from going rogue in 35 seconds
items.summary: OpenAI said Control Room will connect every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. It will work together with its misalignment monitoring systems.

careers.note: Demand snapshot for 2026. ML Engineer is the most in-demand AI title; agentic-AI and deep-learning skills carry the highest pay premiums; Python + one cloud is the baseline. Specialisation beats generalisation for freshers.

paths.note: #1 AI title — build, deploy & maintain models in production. Best all-round entry into AI.
RAG, tool-use & multi-agent systems. ~40% of enterprise apps will embed AI agents by year-end.
Neural nets for vision & speech. Highest premiums; usually needs strong maths / grad study.
Ship & scale models on the cloud. Cloud AI certs add 20–25% to salary.
Foundational, widest entry door; a reliable first step into AI.
Imaging, robotics, autonomous systems, medical AI.
Powers chatbots, search & agents — the hottest application area.
5–8 yrs experience; $140k–$332k bands. Translates AI into business value.
Alignment, evals, red-teaming & policy — newer but expanding fast.

fresher.why: The lingua franca of ML — non-negotiable.
Linear algebra, probability & calculus — enough to reason about models.
Regression, classification, evaluation, the ML workflow.
Build & train neural nets; PyTorch dominates research & jobs.
Ship a small LLM app — the most visible skill to recruiters now.
Real AI work is mostly data; SQL is everywhere.
AWS leads (~40% of postings), then Azure & GCP. Version everything.
A deployed project that solves a real problem is the #1 differentiator.

experienced.why: Docker, CI/CD, monitoring, model/versioning — production is where value lives.
Multi-agent orchestration, tool-use, evals — the surging frontier.
AWS/Azure/GCP architecture; certs add a 20–25% salary premium.
Adapt, measure and harden models for a domain.
Cost & latency engineering for large models.
Trade-offs across data, latency, cost & reliability at scale.
CV, NLP, recsys, healthcare — depth beats breadth at senior levels.
Leading teams and tying models to measurable outcomes.
